packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-19 — UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (blind; no outside source consulted)

Exposure note: nothing in my context proposed an identification or an earlier reading of this text. The
scribe names one authority inside the text ("ph(ilosophu)m p(rim)o methaphisice", side 2 col. 3); I record
that as written and did not use it or anything remembered about a specific work to fill gaps. I made no
attempt to identify the work or author.

=====================================================================
1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image only)
=====================================================================
Observations
- One oblong paper(?) piece, wider than tall, photographed on both sides (image-001 = side 1 with ruler;
  image-008 = side 2). Text upright on both sides. Lower third of the sheet is blank on both sides;
  ragged lower edge; small holes and ink blots at the top edge.
- Four narrow ruled columns across each side, with a wider gap/fold between columns 2 and 3 — i.e. it looks
  like an opened bifolium of a small-format two-column book (tentative). The two outer columns on each side
  are cut by the sheet edge: side 1 col. 1 loses its line beginnings, side 1 col. 4 its line ends; side 2
  col. 1 loses its line beginnings, side 2 col. 4 its line ends. The top line of most columns is trimmed.
- Hand: rapid, very heavily abbreviated current cursive, uneven line spacing, c. 25-30 lines per column.
  Brown-black ink only; no red, no rubrics, no running titles, no enlarged initials. Paragraph marks
  (a large crossed "ff"/paraph-like sign and C-shaped paraphs) open new points. A few interlinear
  insertions and a few struck-through words (noted below). One marginal "ad" between cols. 3 and 4 on
  side 1; a long bracket-stroke in the margin left of side 1 col. 2 (lower part).
- Side 2 col. 2 has only 14 lines of text, then a blank space containing a two-line note in the same or a
  similar hand ("hic spacium ... et nullus / defectus habetur") and below it a single word; the rest of
  the column is empty. Faint pencil/drypoint scribbles in the lower margin of side 1.
Tentative interpretation (not observation)
- Continuous school prose arranged as objections and replies about kinds of argument ("locus a toto
  vniuersali ad partem subiectiuam", "a toto integrali", "a descriptione", "ab interpretatione"), with
  stock example sentences. The note in side 2 col. 2 appears to say a space was left and nothing is missing.
- Column order within a side and which side comes first are NOT established: if this is a bifolium, cols.
  1-2 and cols. 3-4 belong to different leaves and need not be consecutive.

=====================================================================
2. SPANS SELECTED / NOT READ
=====================================================================
Selected (best-preserved, full-width columns): side 1 col. 3 (whole column); side 2 col. 3 (whole column);
side 2 col. 2 (whole, incl. the note); side 1 col. 2 (top two thirds; lower third only in part).
Given only as fragments because the column is physically cut: side 1 col. 1, side 1 col. 4, side 2 col. 1,
side 2 col. 4.
A wider view showing the cut-off outer columns is not available on this sheet; a higher-resolution crop of
side 1 col. 2 lines 1-12 and 20-33 would help most.

Conventions: (..) = proposed expansion; word? = uncertain; [illegible]; [..] = lost at a cut edge, not
supplied. "g°" = the scribe's sign for "ergo". Line numbers are counted from the top of the named column
within the named image, including a trimmed top line; they may be off by one. Overlaps are noted once.
This hand is at the edge of what I can read at this resolution: treat every expansion as a proposal.

8. LIMITATIONS
=====================================================================
- The hand is a fast, highly abbreviated cursive; in many words only the abbreviation skeleton is visible
  and I have proposed the expansion from letter shapes plus the recurring technical vocabulary that the
  page itself repeats legibly elsewhere (toto vniuersali, partem subiectiuam, argumentum, valet, sequitur).
  Words I could not anchor in visible letters are left [illegible] rather than supplied.
- Most secure stretches: side 2 col. 3 L6-L22 and image-013 L5-L10; side 2 col. 2 L5-L14; side 1 col. 3
  L13-L19 and image-006 L5-L11. Least secure: side 1 col. 2 L1-L11 and L20 onward; side 1 col. 3 L1-L12.
- All four outer columns are physically cut; their fragments cannot be completed from this sheet.
- Top lines of several columns are trimmed by the sheet edge.
- Order of columns/leaves and of the two sides is not established.
- Approximate count of physical lines given with at least partial text: c. 190 (of which c. 85 are in the
  four full-width columns; c. 105 are cut-column fragments, 28 of those only as line-end words).
